reading: The grid is cut into panels by separator lines; one rectangle of four lines has background-coloured gaps where those lines cross. The output is that rectangle cut out, its boundary lines included.

new_rows.name: gap_corners
new_rows.datalog: gap_corners(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C), Y1 = Y - 1, cell(Y1, X, S), Y2 = Y + 1, cell(Y2, X, S), X1 = X - 1, cell(Y, X1, S), X2 = X + 1, cell(Y, X2, S).

why: exactly four background cells have all four orthogonal neighbours of one separator colour; their bounding box equals the output
invariants: cell colours inside the box are copied unchanged

reading: The single shape of 8 moves down one row and becomes colour 2.
why: output = input translated by (+1,0) with 8 replaced by 2

reading: Each 5x5 box of 0 (with 8 holes) has a 3x3 interior; every interior 0 cell except the centre is written with a fixed digit by its position: [[1,7,6],[4,-,5],[2,9,3]]. 8 cells and the centre are unchanged.

slots.boxes: each 5x5 rectangle whose border is all 0 (the 0-framed boxes)
slots.code: fixed 3x3 digit table [[1,7,6],[4,centre unchanged,5],[2,9,3]] indexed by position in the box interior
slots.subject: interior cells that are 0 (not the centre)

why: every changed cell is an interior 0 of a box and gets the table digit for its position

reading: Each row has one 5; the whole row is painted by the column of that 5: column 0 -> 2, column 1 -> 4, column 2 -> 3.

slots.marker: the one 5 cell in the row

why: each output row is uniform and its colour depends only on the marker's column

reading: Nine 3x3 jigsaw pieces (grey 5 with coloured corner/edge bits) are scattered on 0; they are assembled into one 9x9 square whose coloured bits form the outer frame, with the all-grey piece in the centre.

slots.pieces: the nine 3x3 objects on the 0 background
slots.placement: each piece goes to the 3x3 slot (corner, edge or centre) matching which of its sides carry colour, so colours lie on the outside of the 9x9

why: the output is the nine input pieces placed without rotation in a 3x3 arrangement

reading: Every 0 cell that belongs to some all-0 2x2 square is painted 2; other cells stay.

new_rows.name: zero_sq
new_rows.datalog:
q(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 0, X1 = X + 1, px(Y, X1, C), Y1 = Y + 1, px(Y1, X, C), px(Y1, X1, C).
zero_sq(Y, X) :- q(Y, X).
zero_sq(Y, X) :- q(Y, X0), X = X0 + 1.
zero_sq(Y, X) :- q(Y0, X), Y = Y0 + 1.
zero_sq(Y, X) :- q(Y0, X0), Y = Y0 + 1, X = X0 + 1.

why: exactly the cells covered by all-0 2x2 squares become 2 (pairs 0,1 exact; pair 2 leaves two such cells at (8,12),(9,12) as 0, an apparent exception)
invariants: 0 cells not in any 2x2 zero square

reading: The single 2 is erased and its four diagonal neighbours get fixed colours: up-left 3, up-right 6, down-left 8, down-right 7 (clipped at the border).
why: the output is the 3x3 pattern [[3,0,6],[0,0,0],[8,0,7]] centred on the marker, everything else 0

reading: Inside the 5-walled region, the longest diagonal run of 0 cells is painted 8 (on a tie, the one lying on the grid's main diagonal/anti-diagonal).

new_rows.name: long_diag
new_rows.datalog:
z(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 0.
rs(1, Y, X) :- z(Y, X), Y0 = Y - 1, X0 = X - 1, !z(Y0, X0).
rs(2, Y, X) :- z(Y, X), Y0 = Y - 1, X0 = X + 1, !z(Y0, X0).
run(D, SY, SX, Y, X) :- rs(D, SY, SX), Y = SY, X = SX.
run(1, SY, SX, Y, X) :- run(1, SY, SX, Y0, X0), Y = Y0 + 1, X = X0 + 1, z(Y, X).
run(2, SY, SX, Y, X) :- run(2, SY, SX, Y0, X0), Y = Y0 + 1, X = X0 - 1, z(Y, X).
len(D, SY, SX, count(Y, X)) :- run(D, SY, SX, Y, X).
best(max(N)) :- len(D, SY, SX, N).
cand(D, SY, SX) :- len(D, SY, SX, N), best(N).
ncand(count(D, SY, SX)) :- cand(D, SY, SX).
w(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
main(1, SY, SX) :- cand(1, SY, SX), SY = SX.
main(2, SY, SX) :- cand(2, SY, SX), w(M), S = SY + SX, S = M.
pick(D, SY, SX) :- cand(D, SY, SX), ncand(K), K = 1.
pick(D, SY, SX) :- main(D, SY, SX), ncand(K), K > 1.
long_diag(Y, X) :- pick(D, SY, SX), run(D, SY, SX, Y, X).

why: the 8 cells form one maximal diagonal run of 0 cells of maximum length; 0 becomes 8, nothing else changes

reading: 2x2 squares of 8 come in pairs on the same two rows; the 2-row strip strictly between each pair is cut out, and the strips are stacked top to bottom.

slots.brackets: pairs of 2x2 all-8 squares sharing the same rows
slots.strip: the 2 rows x columns strictly between the two squares of a pair
slots.output: strips stacked vertically in top-to-bottom order

why: every pair's gap has the same width, and the output equals the strips stacked

reading: Count the 8-connected objects of each colour on the 7 background; output is a bar chart, width 5, height = largest count, with a bottom-aligned bar per colour in fixed columns 5,2,8,9,6 (left to right), height = that colour's object count, rest 7.

slots.count: number of 8-connected single-colour objects per colour

why: each output column c holds count(colour_c) cells of colour_c at the bottom
